question: Can independently developed work on adapters, mixtures of experts, conditional computation, continual learning, program induction and hierarchical reinforcement learning be organized into a common design space for modular deep learning?

key_findings.claim: The survey defines modular deep learning through four largely independent design dimensions.
key_findings.evidence: A modular model separates computation modules from a routing function and an aggregation function, then specifies how all components are trained. Computation may modify parameters, concatenate inputs or compose functions; routing may be fixed or learned, hard or soft, and act at different granularities.

key_findings.claim: The taxonomy exposes common structure across parameter-efficient transfer and conditional-computation systems.
key_findings.evidence: Adapters, LoRA-like parameter composition, prefix/input composition, hypernetworks, task modules and MoE experts can all be represented as choices of module implementation, routing and aggregation. Algorithm 1 gives a common forward-pass recipe.

key_findings.claim: Learned routing has a recurring specialization chicken-and-egg problem.
key_findings.evidence: Routers need useful experts to allocate examples, while experts need stable allocations to specialize. The survey groups resulting failure modes into training instability, module collapse and noise overfitting, rooted in exploration-exploitation and sharing-interference tradeoffs.

key_findings.claim: Hard and soft routing make fundamentally different optimization-efficiency compromises.
key_findings.evidence: Soft mixtures are differentiable but activate all modules unless sparsified. Hard routing localizes updates and supports conditional computation, but discrete choices require reinforcement learning, evolutionary search, stochastic relaxations or top-k approximations; evolutionary routing is explicitly described as brute-force and inefficient.

anchors.section: Soft learned routing and top-k MoE

key_findings.claim: Evidence for modularity is fragmented enough that standardized evaluation is a central open problem.
key_findings.evidence: The conclusion calls for benchmarks spanning downstream quality, parameter/memory cost, latency, compositional generalization and acquisition of new skills, alongside studies of representation modularity, hierarchical modules, learned pretraining routers and structured aggregation.

method.core_idea: Synthesize modular-neural-network research by decomposing every approach into computation, routing, aggregation and training choices, then map uses and failure modes across subfields.
method.mechanism: Define common notation and a generic forward pass; classify parameter, input and function composition; distinguish fixed/learned and hard/soft routing; catalog aggregation and training regimes; and review transfer learning, hierarchical RL, program simulation, causal learning and community module sharing.
assumptions: Functionally specialized, reusable computation is the core meaning of a module.
The four axes are sufficiently independent and expressive to classify most relevant systems.
Results from heterogeneous tasks and modalities are comparable at the design-principle level.
Explicit architectural modularity can promote positive transfer, composition and efficient local updating.

techniques.role: Separates computation, routing, aggregation and training decisions.
Expresses diverse architectures in shared mathematical notation.
Connects transfer learning, MoE, RL, program induction and causal mechanisms.
Organizes instability, collapse and overfitting around common causes.

evaluations.setting: Published modular methods across NLP, vision, speech, reinforcement learning and causal/program systems.
evaluations.metric: Coverage and fit within the four-axis taxonomy.
evaluations.result: The common vocabulary maps many otherwise separate research threads and exposes combinable design choices.

evaluations.setting: Parameter-efficient transfer-learning case studies such as MAD-X and Polytropon.
evaluations.metric: Reported transfer, parameter cost and compositional reuse in cited primary work.
evaluations.result: Fixed or learned modular adapters can reduce storage and support zero-shot recombination, subject to task-specific evidence.
evaluations.baseline: Dense full-model fine-tuning and fully shared multitask learning.

evaluations.metric: Reported quality, active parameters, load balance and training stability.
evaluations.result: Conditional computation scales capacity, while routing collapse and pretraining-to-finetuning transfer remain recurring problems.

evaluations.setting: Hierarchical RL, program simulation and causal-mechanism literature.
evaluations.metric: Qualitative correspondence to reusable modules and routing.
evaluations.result: The taxonomy transfers conceptually, though evaluation protocols and empirical maturity differ substantially by domain.
evaluations.baseline: Monolithic policies and end-to-end undifferentiated networks.

limitations: This is a broad survey, not a controlled meta-analysis; it does not normalize data, compute, parameter count or evaluation quality across cited results.
The definition emphasizes explicit functional specialization, but many papers label parameter blocks 'modules' without demonstrating reuse or independence.
The four axes can interact strongly in practice even though the taxonomy presents them as mutually independent choices.
Coverage ends before recent large-scale open MoE, model-merging and modular-agent work.
Evidence for compositional generalization and causal modularity is thinner than evidence for parameter efficiency.
Application sections inherit publication bias and inconsistent negative-result reporting.
No reproducible benchmark or machine-readable mapping accompanies the survey's call for standardized evaluation.
Community sharing raises compatibility, provenance, security and licensing questions that the architectural taxonomy does not resolve.
failure_modes: Experts collapse because early random routing and specialization reinforce one another.
A router overfits token- or example-level noise and loses out-of-domain performance.
Nominal modules remain entangled and cannot be reused, replaced or locally updated.
Sparse capacity improves pretraining loss but not downstream fine-tuning.
Fixed routing depends on metadata unavailable at deployment.
Aggregation combines incompatible parameters or representations and causes destructive interference.
Efficiency claims omit communication, routing imbalance, storage and serving overhead.
reusable_insights: Treat module computation, routing, aggregation and training as separate interfaces in both code and experiments.
Demonstrate specialization, reuse, composability and local update isolation rather than inferring modularity from architecture names.
Evaluate quality jointly with active parameters, total parameters, memory, communication, latency and load balance.
Test new combinations of known module and routing mechanisms rather than restricting each technique to its original subfield.
Routing benchmarks should include collapse, distribution shift and expert replacement tests.
Versioned module interfaces and provenance are necessary for community-maintained modular ecosystems.
open_questions: Which metrics operationalize functional specialization, reuse and independence across architectures?
Can routers be learned stably from heterogeneous pretraining data without metadata?
How should modules at different abstraction levels be discovered and composed?
Which aggregation rules preserve capabilities when modules are trained separately?
Can modular scaling improve lifecycle cost and safety, not only active FLOPs?
How should shared modules be tested for compatibility, malicious behavior and license provenance?

competitive_landscape.title: Dynamic Neural Networks: A Survey
competitive_landscape.difference: Han et al. organize input-adaptive depth, width and resolution primarily around dynamic computation in vision; this survey uses a broader module/routing/aggregation/training framework spanning transfer, RL, programs and causality.

competitive_landscape.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
competitive_landscape.difference: Switch Transformer demonstrates top-1 expert routing at very large language-model scale and exposes load/stability engineering; the reviewed paper generalizes such systems into one branch of a much wider modular design space.

competitive_landscape.title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP
competitive_landscape.difference: Houlsby et al. establish bottleneck adapters as a practical frozen-backbone transfer method; this survey relates adapters to prefixes, parameter composition, routers and aggregation rather than proposing one PEFT mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: A Survey on Mixture of Experts in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: The later MoE survey provides deeper coverage of expert architecture, routing and systems for LLMs; Modular Deep Learning remains broader and better connects MoE to adapters, continual learning, hierarchical RL and causal modules.

novelty_assessment: The survey's durable contribution is a clean interface-level taxonomy that makes adapters, MoE, options, hypernetworks and program modules comparable. Its breadth is unusually useful for research ideation, but claims that modularity improves transfer or systematic generalization must be traced back to heterogeneous primary studies; the survey itself does not establish those effects experimentally.
reviewer_notes: Read all 76 extracted pages, with detailed checks of the taxonomy, computation forms, learned-routing challenges, hard/soft mechanisms, application summaries, conclusions and future-work agenda. Four primary arXiv comparators or specialized surveys were checked on 2026-08-23.
